_: KR700PA — the kinematic hierarchy, reconstructed from geometry.
The STEP carries no assembly tree: one PRODUCT, zero NEXT_ASSEMBLY_USAGE_OCCURRENCE,
107 MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP, every one unnamed and every one the same green. Everything
below was measured, and the measurements are named so the next person can disagree
with the reasoning rather than with the result.
THE TWO PARALLELOGRAMS. tools/rod-ends.mjs finds each solid's principal axis and the
centroid of its end caps. That gives real attachment points instead of bbox corners,
and two closed loops fall out of them:
LOOP B   elbow -> tieStart(830,2482)              =  ( 410, 297)
Loop A holds the ROCKER at a constant world attitude however the shoulder swings.
Loop B then hangs off the rocker and holds the FLANGE at a constant world attitude
however the boom swings. Together they are why a palletiser's tool plate stays flat
through the entire reach with no controller correcting anything — and why rigging
this as a plain open chain produces a machine that visibly cannot do its job.
PIVOTS ARE DERIVED, NOT COPIED FROM ROD TIPS. A rod's bearing eyes are inset from
its geometric ends — solid 28 runs 1393..2635 between pivots at 1370..2655, inset 23
and 20, symmetrically. Taking the tips as pivots is what makes a linkage that looks
right at rest and comes apart in motion. rearTop and tieEnd are therefore COMPUTED
from the loop closure (RT = E + RB - S, TE = W + TS - E), which makes both loops
exact and means the aim-solved rods never need to stretch to reach.
SOLID ASSIGNMENT IS MEASURED. tools/rig-assign.mjs names a few unmistakable seeds per
link and assigns every other solid to the seed its VERTICES are nearest — not its
centroid, which for a long bracket can sit closer to the wrong link than any part of
the bracket does. It also reports which solids were within 25mm of a rival link;
those were the four bearing caps, which read identically on either side.
Pivots are in the STEP's own millimetres, Z-up. The root carries unitScale and the
Z-up -> Y-up turn, so every number here stays in the frame the survey printed.

links.name: base
links._: The floor slab, the 995 cylinder and the connection boxes behind it. The only thing in the machine allowed to be still.

links.name: column
links._: A1. Solid 41 is centred on (0,0) to within 0.3mm across a 995 diameter, so the axis is measured rather than fitted. Carries the shoulder pivot and, through strut 52 and bracket 27, the rear rod's lower pivot.

links.name: lowerArm
links._: A2. Solid 8 is the tall casting; solid 91 is the rod alongside it, and BOTH span the same two pivots (900 and 2185), so they are one rigid link and not a parallelogram pair.

links.name: boom
links._: A3. The 1681 beam, from x=175 to x=1744 at z~2212 — it extends BEHIND the elbow, which is what a parallelogram needs something to push against. `level: world` means its driven angle is a WORLD attitude, so the shoulder's swing is cancelled for it rather than added to it.

links.name: rocker
links._: The plate across the top, carrying rearTop at one end and tieStart at the other. A SIBLING of the boom on the same elbow pivot, not a child of it: loop A fixes its attitude to the column's, and loop B then hangs off it. This link is the whole mechanism, and the first rig did not have it at all.

links.name: flange
links._: The wrist, at the bearing caps 67/96. Loop B ties its attitude to the rocker's, so it holds level through both the shoulder's and the boom's whole range.

links.name: tool
links._: A4. Solids 16, 98, 99, 100 and 102 are the only ones past the wrist sitting on the machine's centreline (|y| < 10mm), stacked z 1831..2225 — that is a shaft, and its axis is vertical. Because the flange holds level, this axis stays vertical through the whole cycle, which is exactly what lets a palletiser square a box to a pallet.

links.name: rearRod
links._: Loop A's rod. Its orientation is SOLVED from both attachment pivots every frame, not inherited as a child rotation — that is the difference between a rod and a rod that floats off its joint. rearTop is computed as E + RB - S so the span is exactly the arm's 1285 and the rod never has to stretch to reach.

links.name: tieRod
links._: Loop B's rod. Solid 17 spans 806..2153 and its pivots are 830..2130 — inset 24 and 23, symmetrically, which is what a clevis end looks like. tieEnd is computed as W + TS - E so the span is exactly the boom's 1300.

paint._: Linear. Renders sRGB #C0521A — a deeper, redder industrial orange than the amber the first pass produced. tokens.css derives the interface accent from this value, so the two move together or the derivation becomes a false claim about the artefact.
